data.source_title: Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention, 2026 Update
data.locator: Chapter 9, Emergency Department Management of Exacerbations (Adults, Adolescents, Children 6–11 years), pp. 184–186; Chapter 12, children 5 years and younger, Box 12-3, p. 219.
data.source_setting: Acute-care/emergency assessment; GINA distinguishes children 6–11 years and children 5 years and younger.
value: Take a brief history and perform examination concurrently with prompt therapy; assess severity, vital signs/oxygen saturation, response to treatment, risk factors, and alternative or additional causes of breathlessness.
For children under 18, consider a validated assessment tool such as PRAM; monitor oxygen saturation and, where feasible without delaying care, lung function before treatment and during response.

For children 5 and younger, features such as inability to speak/drink, cyanosis, respiratory rate above 40/min, room-air oxygen saturation below 92%, or quiet chest are immediate hospital-transfer indicators in the GINA box.
data.source_evidence_basis: GINA 2026 text under ED management specifies concurrent brief history/physical exam and prompt therapy, severity/vital-sign assessment, differential causes, objective assessment, and PRAM consideration for under-18s. Box 12-3 provides the listed under-5 transfer indicators.
data.limitations: The under-5 transfer signs are age-specific and must not be generalized to older children. This record deliberately omits treatment doses; GINA itself notes oximetry limitations including potential overestimation in people with dark skin and altitude adjustments.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use age-banded cases to represent assessment, escalation, response reassessment, and disposition; do not turn the guideline into an autonomous treatment order.
data.applicability: Pediatric acute asthma exacerbation assessment in acute care; distinguish age bands and assess competing diagnoses.
data.source_period: 2026 Strategy Report; GINA announced the report in May 2026. No patient cohort period applies.
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
